uncited: Inside/Outside Inversion is a post-processing or configuration step in volumetric rendering that swaps the semantic definition of "interior" and "exterior" relative to a surface threshold.
It solves the problem of ambiguous or inverted volume data where the default assumption (values above threshold are inside) does not match the physical or logical reality of the dataset.
It distinguishes itself from [Inside-Outside Voxelization](3081-inside-outside-voxelization.md) by operating on the scalar field interpretation rather than the geometric voxelization process itself.
The input is a scalar volume grid $V$ and a threshold value $T$.
The output is a modified interpretation of the volume where the boolean classification of voxels as "inside" or "outside" is inverted.
The method modifies the evaluation logic or a boolean mask $M$ derived from $V$.
Evaluate the scalar value $v$ at the current voxel.
Let $I(v, T)$ be the indicator function for the inside region.
Using strict inequality ($>$) vs non-strict ($\ge$) affects boundary voxels.
It differs from simple volume inversion by affecting surface normal orientation for shading rather than just the binary inside/outside mask for ray marching or voxelization.
- If threshold $T < 0$: Treat the side toward larger/more positive values as outside.
- If threshold $T > 0$: Treat the side toward smaller/more negative values as outside.
No additional memory is required beyond the flag.
Linear with the number of voxels evaluated.
Use when the default "high value = inside" assumption is physically incorrect for the dataset.
It is commonly used in scientific visualization where scalar fields represent physical quantities with inherent signs (positive/negative).
